rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-evidence/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, so `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.workflow` applies to it as a site.

The requirement has two obligations for each site. The skill must open with its workflow, before any other section. The workflow must be written as ordered steps.

- **Placement.** The first section after the `# Habeas evidence` title is `## Workflow`. It comes before `## Rules`, `## Fixing findings`, `## Disagreeing assessments` and `## Gotchas`. Before `## Workflow` there is only the title's lead-in: a short paragraph and a three-item list that defines the `true`, `false` and FIXME judgments. This lead-in is not a separate section. It is the opening text of the H1 section, and every other bundled skill has the same shape, a short lead-in followed by `## Workflow` as the first `##` heading. The text says "before any other section", which is naturally read as a heading-level rule. A stricter reading, that no prose may precede the workflow, is not equally supported by that wording. Under the stricter reading every bundled skill would fail.
- **Ordered steps.** The workflow is a checklist of numbered steps, `- [ ] 1.` through `- [ ] 8.`, in the order to perform them.

No violation queries were listed for this site, so there are no matches to judge. I found no gap.
